question: In the summer of 2026, Campania’s Terra dei fuochi (Land of Fires) was hit with new waste fires. In Giugliano, following a fire on 6 September 2026, the Campania Regional Environmental Protection Agency (ARPAC) found dioxin concentrations above the scientific reference values. In Caivano, urgent measures were taken following repeated exceedances of the daily PM10 emission limit value.

The Cannavacciuolo and Others v. Italy ECtHR judgment of 30 January 2025 established that residents’ right to life had been breached, and imposed general preventive measures, independent monitoring and public information. Directives 2008/50/EC and (EU) 2024/2881 set out, respectively, existing obligations and the revised European air quality framework. In the light of the above: 1.

What information does the Commission have on compliance with the PM10 limit values and on whether the air quality plans in the areas in question are fit for purpose, pursuant to Articles 13 and 23 of Directive 2008/50/EC?
Are the European monitoring tools up to the task of assessing the exposure of the population to toxic pollutants when waste fires are recurrent, and what improvements could be made?
In the period since an answer was given to question E-000763/2025, have the new incidents led to further requests for information from Italy or checks on compliance with EU environmental legislation?
